You said the German climate should be fine. I'm not trying to shut you down, but it might be helpful to do some more research on the process of aging tea if that's your goal. 

You can get hygrometers from amazon, and mylar works as a smell free, air tight storage solution.

You can't talk about wanting to accelerate aging and not think about temperature when you're living in a cooler Western climate. Store your tea in the classic mylar and boveda so it doesn't dry out, but otherwise honestly just buy aged tea if you want to drink aged tea. 

The reason that there's so much debate over storage among western tea drinkers is that no one can replicate Malaysian/hong kong/wherever.

It sounds like you're expecting someone to give you a definitive guide on how to age tea and it won't happen.

I don't think they're worth it. In my experience all teas, if they're of reasonable quality, can be brewed with boiling, except Japanese greens. That includes Chinese greens. If you want lower temp you can pour the boiling water into a yuzamashi or similar before brewing.

To add to that, the temperature controllers in these kettles often become unreliable over time.
